title: Growing a Disk Without Downtime: Cloud Volume, Partition, LVM, Filesystem
intro: The database volume is 95% full. In the cloud you can grow the disk in seconds, but the operating system doesn't use the new space until you grow each layer: partition, LVM physical volume, logical volume, filesystem. All of it can be done online. This host's 100GB volume was just resized to 200GB in the cloud console.

steps.prompt: Look at the block device layers.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                MAJ:MIN RM  SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINTS
nvme1n1             259:4    0  200G  0 disk
└─nvme1n1p1         259:5    0  100G  0 part
  └─vg_data-lv_pg   253:0    0  100G  0 lvm  /var/lib/postgresql
steps.explanation: The disk is 200G, but the partition and the logical volume are still 100G.
steps.why: Each layer must be grown, bottom up: disk, partition, PV, LV, filesystem. Skip one and 'df' stays unchanged, a very common confusion after resizing a cloud volume.

steps.prompt: Grow partition 1 of /dev/nvme1n1 to fill the disk.
steps.fake_output: CHANGED: partition=1 start=2048 old: size=209713119 end=209715167 new: size=419428319 end=419430367
steps.why: growpart (from cloud-utils) edits the partition table safely while it's in use. Note the space between device and partition number: 'growpart /dev/nvme1n1 1', not 'nvme1n1p1'.

steps.prompt: Tell LVM the physical volume /dev/nvme1n1p1 got bigger.
steps.fake_output:
Physical volume "/dev/nvme1n1p1" changed
  1 physical volume(s) resized or updated / 0 physical volume(s) not resized
steps.explanation: The volume group vg_data now has 100G free.
steps.why: LVM's value is exactly this flexibility: logical volumes can grow, span several disks, or be snapshotted, independently of physical partitions. 'vgs' now shows the free space.

steps.prompt: Grow the logical volume /dev/vg_data/lv_pg into all free space, resizing its filesystem in the same step.
steps.fake_output:
Size of logical volume vg_data/lv_pg changed from 100.00 GiB to 200.00 GiB.
  Logical volume vg_data/lv_pg successfully resized.
meta-data=/dev/mapper/vg_data-lv_pg isize=512 agcount=4, agsize=6553600 blks
data blocks changed from 26214400 to 52428800
steps.explanation: The LV and its XFS filesystem are both 200G now.
steps.why: -r (--resizefs) runs the right filesystem tool for you: xfs_growfs for XFS, resize2fs for ext4. Without it you'd have to run that separately. XFS can only grow, never shrink, so don't over-allocate expecting to take space back.

steps.prompt: Confirm the filesystem sees the new size.
steps.fake_output:
Filesystem                 Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/mapper/vg_data-lv_pg  200G   95G  105G  48% /var/lib/postgresql
steps.why: Always verify at the top layer, because df is what the application sees. Then fix the real problem: alert at 80% with a growth forecast (predict_linear, sre-tutorial-004), not at 95%.
